question: Which vessels due at Rotterdam next week are most likely to miss their berth window, and why?

thinking: The week runs from Monday 2 November to Sunday 8 November 2026, so I'll pull the port lookup, arrivals, source coverage and congestion for that window.

I'm going to check the incidents for these voyages quickly, starting with VG-1088 and the Rio Verde voyage, which hasn't departed yet. The Rio Verde origin at BRSSZ has congestion I haven't verified, so I'll look into that along with the incident and message records.

headline.text: MV Arctic Fern (VG-1088) is the most likely to miss its Rotterdam berth window: its revised ETA is already 23 hours after the window closes. MV Kestrel Bay and MV Celtic Dawn are next, both with unverified engine reports. MV Rio Verde carries extra uncertainty because it has not yet sailed.

interpretation.text: 'Next week' is Mon 2026-11-02 to Sun 2026-11-08, port-local dates at NLRTM. This gives six voyages due. 'Miss the window' means the revised ETA falls after the berth window end, or is at risk of doing so.

confirmed_facts.text: MV Arctic Fern (V007, from SGSIN) has a revised ETA of 2026-11-04T14:00Z. Its berth window closes 2026-11-03T15:00Z, so the ETA is after the window end. Status is Delayed, with a 33 h slip.

The Arctic Fern's delay is explained by a Confirmed incident, hull fouling / speed loss, reported by the technical manager. The incident attributes 33 h of delay, which matches the full recorded slip.

The other five voyages show a revised ETA 10 h before their window end, with no slip recorded: Northern Lark VG-1097, Kestrel Bay VG-1091, Amber Coast VG-1099, Celtic Dawn VG-1102 and Rio Verde VG-1095.
Rotterdam congestion is High, with an average wait of 36 h and 25 vessels at anchor on 2026-10-26. This is a port-wide figure, not a fact about any one vessel.

unverified_reports.text: Kestrel Bay (V008): the crew reported that the No. 2 auxiliary engine tripped twice. The incident INC-224 has status Reported, with no attributed delay hours. The crew also said the vessel 'may need parts in Rotterdam' and had 'no speed loss so far'. None of this is independently verified.
Celtic Dawn (V012): the master reported a main engine fuel pump fault, INC-219, with status Reported. No delay hours are attributed (null, not zero).

inferences.text: Ranking by risk: (1) Arctic Fern, because its ETA is already past the window. (2) Kestrel Bay, because the possible need for parts in Rotterdam could prolong its stay, though its 10 h of margin and the reported absence of speed loss limit the arrival risk. (3) Celtic Dawn, because of an unresolved fuel pump fault with 10 h of margin. (4) Rio Verde, because it has not sailed and its Brazilian origin has no recent congestion data. (5) Northern Lark and Amber Coast, which have no recorded issues.
inferences.based_on: Voyage ETA vs window end, incident status, and the absence of incidents on other voyages. Vessel evidence is kept separate from port-wide context.

inferences.text: Rotterdam's High congestion (36–40 h average waits over 2026-10-20 to 26) could push even on-time vessels past their windows if berths are not free on arrival. This is port-wide context. It would matter most for vessels with thin margins, and it is a projection, not a vessel fact.
inferences.based_on: Port-wide congestion trend, which is not specific to any vessel.

data_gaps.text: The congestion feed for Santos (BRSSZ), Rio Verde's origin, ends on 2026-10-04. Conditions there are unknown. Rio Verde (VG-1095) departs 2026-10-27, after the snapshot.
The messages/extra folder was not loaded (45 files), so some reports may be missing.

recommended_checks.text: Ask Nordwave Marine whether Arctic Fern can recover speed, and whether a later berth window at Rotterdam can be rebooked, since the ETA is 23 h past the window.
Get confirmation from Kestrel Bay's master or technical manager on the auxiliary engine fault and on whether parts or repairs at Rotterdam are needed.
Ask Celtic Dawn's master for the status and expected delay of the fuel pump fault.
